# Payment records and DTO service

> The `Payment` database model and [`PaymentDtoService`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-dto.service.ts#L13), the small data-access layer other code uses to create, update and look up payments.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

A payment is one row in the `Payment` table. It has an id (a UUIDv7 made by the database), an `idempotencyKey` (the key that makes a charge safe to retry), an amount, a status, the user, the order it belongs to (`bisOrderId`) and a `providerRef` (the Stripe [`PaymentIntent`](../../../../packages/payments/internal/stripe/stripe.go#L32) id, once known). A payment also has many ledger entries, linked by `paymentId`. See [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md) for those. Statuses are `PENDING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUNDED` and `UNKNOWN`. `UNKNOWN` means the Stripe call timed out, so the charge may or may not exist. The code must ask Stripe about it later and never blindly re-send. [Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN](resolving-unknown-payments.md) covers that. Other code does not touch the model directly. It injects [`PaymentDtoService`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-dto.service.ts#L13), which wraps the model. Reads go through one Sequelize scope, `WithAll`. You pass a filter object and the scope builds the `where` clause. It can also join the order and apply the order's own filters. Writes take a transaction, so callers decide what commits together. [`PaymentDtoModule`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/payment-dto.module.ts#L18) registers the model and exports the service. The `payments` index re-exports both. [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md) is the main user.

**Look at:** [`Payment` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L23) · [`PaymentDtoService` in payment-dto.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-dto.service.ts#L13) · [`PaymentDtoModule` in payment-dto.module.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/payment-dto.module.ts#L18) · [index.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/index.ts)

## Pieces

- [Payment status values](payment-status.md): The `PaymentStatus` enum, which lists the states a payment can be in, including `UNKNOWN` for timed-out provider calls.
- [The WithAll query scope and its filters](with-all-scope.md): A Sequelize scope that turns a `PaymentWithAllFilters` object (id, idempotency key, status, amount, attributes, order filters) into a `where` clause and an optional order join.
- Lazy import of the orders domain: The model loads the orders domain only when needed, to avoid a circular-load problem between orders and payments.
- [Payment data service](payment-dto-service.md): Injectable service with `countAll`, `findAll`, `findOne`, `requestPayment`, `requestPayments`, `requestPaymentOptional`, `create` and `update`.
- Nest module for the payment service: Registers the `Payment` model and exports [`PaymentDtoService`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-dto.service.ts#L13) for other modules.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payment` | Table behind the `Payment` model. It has an index on `userId` plus `id` descending, named `idx_payment_user_id_desc`. [`PaymentDtoService`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payment-dto.service.ts#L13) reads and writes it. |
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | Linked from `Payment` as `ledgerEntries` through `paymentId`. It is only declared as an association here. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): A payment owns ledger entries through the `ledgerEntries` association.

## Watch out

- `requestPayment` throws [`Fatal_NotFoundError`](../common-errors/errors.md) when nothing matches. `findOne` returns `null`. Use `requestPaymentOptional` if you want `null` instead of an error.
- `update` uses a `where` clause and throws [`Fatal_NotFoundError`](../common-errors/errors.md) if no row changed. It is not a silent no-op.
- The `additors` option on `requestPayment` and `requestPayments` only accepts `{ type: 'stub' }`, which does nothing. Any other type throws `BadRequestException`.
- The scope treats falsy filter values as absent, so `amount: 0` is ignored. Other domains import the model from the `payments` index, which the index file itself marks as transitional debt.
